title: Rollback restores configuration without waiting for stream shutdown
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a rollback waits until OBS reports the stream stopped before it restores anything' (VAL-114), 'a rollback sends nothing after a stop that stays active, and names every step it skipped', 'a rollback whose stream state cannot be read treats the stream as active and sends nothing more', 'a StopStream OBS rejects is not a failure once the stream is confirmed stopped, and the rollback goes on', 'a StopStream OBS rejects while the stream stays active is reported with the stop failure', 'a start that timed out may have been applied, so the rollback stops it and checks before it restores', 'a setup whose stream cannot be confirmed stopped says its rollback is incomplete and restores nothing' (configureObsStream; guard that passed before and after: 'a stop that timed out is not journaled, so a rollback does not report a start OBS would refuse')
proof: Holds. rollback() replayed the journal with one raw sendRequest per step, so the StopStream inverse of a forward StartStream (journaled last, so run first) was treated as finished the moment OBS answered, and SetVideoSettings, SetStreamServiceSettings and the profile restores were sent at once; unlike stopActiveStream it never polled GetStreamStatus. The tests drive createObsConfigurationTransaction with a scripted request function and an injected delay and clock, and compare request order. On the unchanged code the order test failed: after StopStream the next requests were SetVideoSettings, SetStreamServiceSettings, StartStream, with the three expected GetStreamStatus polls missing; the stuck-active test sent all three restores where only four status polls were expected; the unreadable-status test (a throwing request, a refused request, an answer without data, an answer without outputActive) did the same; and the configureObsStream test returned the plain 'streaming stopped immediately' message with no 'Rollback incomplete'. Fix: a shared waitForStreamInactive (also used by stopActiveStream, whose behaviour is unchanged: 250 ms x 10 polls, an unreadable status still counts as stopped there) polls after every StopStream inverse in rollback in fail-closed mode: only outputActive === false with outputReconnecting !== true confirms idle; a throwing, refused, empty or malformed status counts as still active. If idle is not confirmed within stopPollIntervalMs x stopPollAttempts (250 x 10 by default) rollback() resolves with 'StopStream: output still active after <ms>ms' or 'StopStream: stream state unknown' (preceded by the rejection comment when OBS refused the stop) and one 'skipped <requestType>' per remaining step, and sends nothing else; a StopStream OBS refuses while the polls show the output idle is not a failure and the rollback goes on. The bounds, the delay function and the clock are options of createObsConfigurationTransaction (configureObsStream passes them through a new optional transactionOptions). Also: a StartStream that throws after dispatch (timeout) is now journaled with its StopStream inverse, so the new gate covers a start OBS applied late; a timed-out StopStream is deliberately still not journaled (its inverse StartStream would be refused as already active and reported as a failed rollback).

title: Rollback restarts the stream right after restoring video settings, skipping the settle delay the forward path uses to avoid an OBS crash
test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a rollback starts the stream again only after the video settle time has passed since the last video restore' (VAL-115), 'a video color restore counts for the settle time, and other restores and a missing video restore do not'
proof: Holds. The forward path waits 1200 ms before StartStream because starting the encoder while the video output is being reinitialised can crash OBS in video_output_connect2; rollback sent the StartStream inverse (the inverse of the first journaled mutation, so the last step) directly after the SetVideoSettings and Video-category SetProfileParameter restores. The tests use an injected delay that moves a fake clock and a request log stamped with that clock. On the unchanged code the first failed with 'StartStream came 500ms after the video restore' (only a 500 ms restore in between, no wait), the second with an empty list of delays where [1200] was expected for a Video/ColorRange restore. Fix: rollback() remembers the clock time after the last video-affecting restore (SetVideoSettings, or SetProfileParameter with parameterCategory 'Video'; also when the restore's answer never came, since OBS may have applied it) and, before a StartStream inverse, awaits the rest of videoSettleMs (1200 by default, via the injected delay). With a 500 ms restore in between only the remaining 700 ms is waited; an Output-category restore or no video restore waits nothing. The forward delay(1200) now uses the same VIDEO_SETTLE_MS constant.
